cands.name: Pamala Bivins
cands.bio: Democrat, 71; pastor of Mount Moriah AME Church in Wildwood and former Wildwood city commissioner (25 years per campaign site). Born and raised in Wildwood.
cands.local_ties: Born and raised in Wildwood (campaign site).

record.text: Withdrew from the March 2026 special election for this seat before qualifying closed (Florida Politics), but qualified for the November general election.
Campaign site credits her with parks and recreation projects during her time on the Wildwood commission.

cands.gaps: Did not respond to the voter guide. No donors, endorsements or news coverage found; her campaign site has only a text graphic, not a clean headshot. Sources give her name as Pamala Kaye Bivins and once as Pamela Harrison-Bivins. Owner sources: only alexjoneslive.com on-site search was run for this name (no results); stewpeters.com, rumble.com and infowars.com on-site searches are bot-blocked and the web-search budget ran out, so those were not checked.

cands.name: Samantha Scott
cands.bio: Republican, age 45; House member since March 25, 2026 (elected unopposed in a special election). Lifelong Sumter County resident, chair of the Sumter County Republican Party, marketing director for Mike Scott Plumbing.

record.text: Appointed by Gov. DeSantis to the Lake-Sumter State College District Board of Trustees in 2025; elected to the House when no other candidate qualified for the special election.
Voted for the joint resolution that put Amendment 3 (property taxes) on the November 2026 ballot, per the News Collaborative guide.

endorsements.text: U.S. Rep. Daniel Webster, CFO Blaise Ingoglia, several House Republicans, Sumter County Sheriff Pat Breeden, Associated Industries of Florida, Florida Fraternal Order of Police; Americans for Prosperity-Florida praised her.

cands.gaps: Did not complete the voter guide. Short voting record. No donor reporting retrieved; no controversies found. Owner sources: only alexjoneslive.com on-site search was run for this name (no results); stewpeters.com, rumble.com and infowars.com on-site searches are bot-blocked and the web-search budget ran out, so those were not checked.

votes.what: Joint resolution putting Amendment 3 (Save Our Homes property-tax changes: higher homestead exemption, lower assessment-increase limits) on the Nov 2026 ballot.
